open_points.subject: Activation after trial-corpus growth
open_points.text: K-05 says a captured case is "the trial case every later implementation must pass"; M06 says "every implementation of a contract version must pass"; M09 says the current activation is simply the activation recorded last and names no invalidation when the corpus grows.
open_points.question: When a trial case is added, what happens if the currently activated implementation has no admitted verdict over the enlarged corpus, and may a run still start with it?
options: Keep the existing activation usable; only later admissions and rollbacks must cover the enlarged corpus
Invalidate the activation until that implementation or another one is admitted over the enlarged corpus
Automatically readmit the activated implementation over the enlarged corpus
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing activation usable, because State 0 says every later implementation must pass and defines no deactivation action.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity
open_points.text: M08 says "a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict," but its facts include freshly minted TrialExecutions and `decided_at`, and "every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time."
open_points.question: If admission is performed again for the same implementation and corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict returned, or is a new verdict with new TrialExecutions created; and which of those observations are identity facts?
options: Return the existing verdict and do not rerun the cases
Rerun the cases but replace or amend the existing verdict
Create a distinct admission verdict for each admission run
Treat verdict identity as only implementation plus corpus while retaining multiple evidence sets separately
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing verdict for the same implementation and corpus, because M08 explicitly declares it to be the same value.

open_points.subject: try an implementation
open_points.text: The primary action says only "try an implementation" with output "trial evidence per case"; unlike admission, it does not say whether it runs the whole active corpus or selected cases.
open_points.question: Which TrialExecutions does one try action create: one for every active case, one caller-selected case, or a caller-selected subset?
options: Every active trial case of the implementation's contract version
An explicitly selected subset of trial cases
open_points.default_guess: Run every active trial case, interpreting "trial evidence per case" as evidence for the whole corpus.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution actor
open_points.text: K-15 says "The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record," but M07 has no requesting or executing actor even though TrialExecutions arise both from an agent's try action and from kernel-run admission.
open_points.question: What actor or cause must a TrialExecution record carry so manual trials can be attributed to the requesting agent and admission trials to the kernel?
options: Carry `executed_by` as the requesting agent or kernel
Carry separate trigger and requester facts, such as `trigger: try|admission` and `requested_by`
Treat every TrialExecution as a kernel action and do not record which agent requested a manual trial
open_points.default_guess: Carry the trigger and the requesting actor, using the kernel actor for admission executions.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution file output
open_points.text: K-14 says "Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`," while M07 says a successful file output records "only its facts — digest, size and media type" and is never a StoredValue.
open_points.question: Does each file output in TrialExecution also carry its disclosure class, or is that class deliberately omitted and derived from the trial inputs when read?
options: Derive the class from the trial case inputs and specify that it is not stored
Treat trial file outputs as outside the rule that every value carries a class

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt after `not_sent`
open_points.text: M26 says every non-read send, including `draft-write`, has an EffectAttempt whose authority may be a flow activation, but its lifecycle says "A `not_sent` attempt leaves its approval unused, so a resume sends a new attempt under it."
open_points.question: Under what authority is a `draft-write` retried after `not_sent`, since its original authority is a flow activation rather than an approval?
options: Retry under the same flow activation that authorized the original attempt
Use whichever original authority the attempt recorded, with the unused-approval rule applying only to approval-authorized attempts
open_points.default_guess: Use the original recorded authority: the same flow activation for `draft-write`, and the same unused approval for an approval-authorized attempt.
